source.description: Profile field encryption (name, about, about emoji, phone-number-sharing boolean, payment address), profile avatar stream encryption, the unidentified-access verifier, and end-to-end decoding of profile responses, as done by signal-cli v0.14.7. See spec/crypto/profile-cipher.md. All hex is lowercase. 'k1'/'k2' name the 32-byte profile keys in 'keys'. Nonces are fixed by the vector author (a real client draws them at random); ciphertext = nonce(12) || AES-256-GCM ciphertext || tag(16), key = the 32-byte profile key, no associated data.
source.signal_service_java: https://github.com/Turasa/libsignal-service-java @ v2.15.3_unofficial_151 (66956cb4a0394d50cee3590209baf58312084a44), the version bundled with signal-cli 0.14.7
source.provenance: Derived offline by the spec agent on 2026-10-25 with jshell (Temurin 25.0.5) over the reference distribution class path /work/third_party/signal-cli-0.14.7/lib/*. Fixed-nonce ciphertexts were produced with the JDK's own AES/GCM/NoPadding and then checked against the reference decoders (signal-service-java ProfileCipher.decryptString/decryptBoolean/decryptWithLength, ProfileCipherInputStream, and signal-cli ProfileUtils.decryptProfile); 'reference_encrypt_string' entries were produced by the reference ProfileCipher.encryptString (random nonce) and re-derived with the JDK cipher. 'padding_targets' come from ProfileCipher.getTargetNameLength/getTargetAboutLength. 'decode_profile' results are the field values of the Profile object returned by ProfileUtils.decryptProfile for the given response JSON (null result = the reference decoder returned null). The PUT body string is the reference JsonUtil serialization of a SignalServiceProfileWrite. No network access. None of this is an upstream test vector; upstream publishes none for these primitives.

decrypt_string_quirks.case: trailing NUL stripped (given Bob, family empty)
wrong key (k2) on the first quirk ciphertext

boolean_fields.note: plaintext byte 0x02 decodes as true (any non-zero first byte)

payment_address.signature_note: the 64-byte signature inside the proto is an XEdDSA signature (random nonce) by the identity private key over the raw public-address bytes; any valid signature is acceptable, so this exact value is reproducible only by verification

avatar.case: tag tampered (last byte xor 1) on avatar case 0

decode_profile.case: given Bob with empty family (trailing NUL)
name ciphertext tampered: whole decode fails
name not base64: only that field is null
name shorter than 29 bytes: whole decode fails
version not found on server (encrypted fields absent)
payment address signed by a different key: dropped
payment address length prefix too large: dropped
payment address shorter than 29 bytes: whole decode fails

put_profile_body.note: Field ciphertexts are the fixed-nonce values from decode_profile 'complete profile'; avatar=true,sameAvatar=false means a new avatar follows. A real client uses fresh random nonces. version/commitment are deterministic for (key, ACI).
